found.title: File:Croeso I Gymru-Welcome to Wales - geograph.org.uk - 282024.jpg
found.credit: From geograph.org.uk
found.desc: Croeso I Gymru/Welcome to Wales This nice old sign once resided very close to the border by the Anchor Hotel. Its removal by the council caused an outcry and it was eventually returned to an insignificant location in a layby some 100 metres from the border. It now has to fight for recognition with a street light (plus Christmas decorations), and advertising hoardings for a Saab dealership and a Shell petrol station. The odd angle of the shot is the only way to do some sort of justice to the sign without including all the other items.

found.title: File:Amiable Sheep - geograph.org.uk - 361967.jpg
found.credit: From geograph.org.uk
found.desc: Amiable Sheep When I arrived at this location I was intrigued by how docile the local sheep were - they ran to the car as I arrived and were almost jumping over themselves when I pulled the camera out of its bag. The reason became apparent almost immediately. I was only there for a couple of minutes but three separate individuals turned up with scraps to feed them. It seems that this is a spot where locals come to feed the sheep...

found.title: File:Croeso i Gymru - geograph.org.uk - 744105.jpg
found.credit: From geograph.org.uk
found.desc: Croeso i Gymru The welcome to Wales seems superfluous as traffic passing this sign has almost certainly come from Wales. The way that the boundary between Montgomeryshire and Shropshire falls here results in passing from England to Wales in a west -east direction. The small area of Shropshire that the A489 has just passed through is effectively an island, there being no road connection to the rest of the county without passing through Powys.
